decision_reason: A1 already represents intensity, periodicity, posture, rotation, translation, smoothness, and impacts, but motion_regularity is constant across all split classes and provides no discrimination. The weakest-covered unseen activity, jump front & back, benefits from explicit gravity-axis translation and directional-persistence concepts that distinguish jumping from progressive jogging and running while retaining climbing stairs as a seen transfer anchor. Knees bending (crouching) is close to waist bends forward and gains a transferable body-region distinction based on lower-limb versus trunk or arm motion.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: lower_limb_motion_dominance
attributes.definition: Degree to which dynamic motion is concentrated at the ankle and lower leg relative to motion of the chest and forearm.

levels.Low: Little lower-limb motion or motion dominated by the trunk or upper limb.
levels.Medium: Lower-limb and upper-body motion have comparable prominence.
levels.High: Motion is strongly dominated by the ankle and lower leg.

attributes.name: vertical_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of translational body motion along the gravity axis, including repeated upward and downward displacement.

levels.Low: Little translation along the gravity axis.
levels.Medium: Moderate or secondary translation along the gravity axis.
levels.High: Strong, repeated, or dominant translation along the gravity axis.

attributes.name: directional_persistence
attributes.definition: Degree to which translational motion maintains a consistent progression direction instead of remaining local or repeatedly reversing direction.

levels.Low: Little directional progression or frequent reversal of translation.
levels.Medium: Partly persistent or intermittently reversing directional progression.
levels.High: Sustained translation with a consistent progression direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a direct and transferable distinction between sedentary postures, moderate articulated actions, and vigorous locomotor activities.
Repetition rate separates static activities and moderate-rate actions from faster cyclic motion, with walking, cycling, and running providing seen cadence anchors.
Sustained rapid fluctuation is physically distinct from isolated impacts and helps characterize the continuous articulated motion of crouching versus the rougher dynamics of jumping.
Short high-magnitude changes provide a clear impact contrast between jumping and non-impact bending activities, with running supplying a seen high-impact anchor.
Mean gravity-relative posture is essential for transferring the ordered upright, inclined, and horizontal distinctions represented by standing, sitting, and lying.
Global posture change separates repeated crouching from fixed postures and remains distinct from local limb rotation.
Angular-motion prominence remains useful for distinguishing articulated bending and pedaling from static posture and primarily progressive locomotion.
Overall sustained progression remains a fundamental distinction between local bending or static posture and locomotor activities.
All supplied A1 class prototypes assign the same High level, so this concept provides no split-specific class contrast despite being physically measurable.

Body-region motion distribution adds an independent distinction between lower-limb-driven crouching and trunk-dominant waist bending or arm-dominant elevation. The ankle, chest, and forearm inventory supports this contrast, while climbing stairs and cycling provide lower-limb seen anchors.

Gravity-axis translation captures the pronounced upward-downward displacement of jumping and separates it from mainly forward jogging. Climbing stairs supplies a seen example with meaningful vertical progression, while running provides a vigorous locomotor comparison.

Translation magnitude alone does not distinguish sustained forward locomotion from repeated front-back reversal. Directional persistence directly separates the low-U_NN jogging and jump front & back pair, with walking and running serving as seen progressive-motion anchors.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes are complementary rather than duplicate. Motion_intensity measures aggregate energy; smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation; impulsiveness measures isolated abrupt peaks. Cadence measures repetition rate and does not duplicate any retained predictability attribute because the nondiscriminative motion_regularity concept was dropped. Posture_inclination measures mean global orientation, whereas posture_variability measures its change over time. Rotational_motion and translational_motion separate angular motion from linear progression. Vertical_translation refines the gravity-axis component without replacing total translational prominence, and directional_persistence describes whether translation maintains direction rather than its magnitude or axis. Lower_limb_motion_dominance describes the anatomical distribution of dynamic motion and is distinct from global posture and total energy.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
